claims.mechanism: Every project entity is source-addressable and belongs to exactly one query-conditioned exact or aggregate representation; effective omitted influence is bounded rather than declared merely nonzero.
claims.operating_regime: all project sizes and model boundaries
claims.primary_metric: valid total cover plus effective-influence receipt

claims.mechanism: A hierarchy antichain plus disjoint residual exceptions represents every leaf exactly once.
claims.decision: retain as an invariant; do not interpret as usefulness

claims.mechanism: Exact budgeted tree dynamic programming using oracle cell mass gives the minimum squared field error available under a representation-unit budget.
claims.operating_regime: small oracle-sized hierarchies with uniform-within-cell reconstruction
claims.baseline: coarsest root cover and greedy refinement
claims.minimum_effect: error is nonincreasing with budget and reaches zero at leaf resolution
claims.decision: retain as a mathematical ceiling, not a deployable retriever

claims.mechanism: Immediate value-of-refinement ignores discrete child costs and complementary future refinements, so it need not minimize field error under a unit budget.
claims.operating_regime: finite hierarchy covers with nonuniform oracle mass
claims.minimum_effect: one deterministic strict counterexample falsifies universal optimality
claims.decision: reject one-step greedy optimality; retain it only as a speed baseline

claims.mechanism: A cover selected to minimize uniform-cell L2 error need not improve L1 error after the budget increases.
claims.operating_regime: finite hierarchy covers with objective-specific optimization
claims.primary_metric: L1 delta under an L2-optimal budget increase
claims.minimum_effect: one deterministic strict counterexample falsifies metric-independent monotonicity
claims.decision: require one preregistered objective and report all non-optimized metrics separately

claims.mechanism: A bounded-arity path hierarchy optimized greedily for L2 reconstruction plus 0.01 times unresolved influence mass transfers an equal-token resolution-recall gain across projects.
claims.operating_regime: GraphGraph development plus frozen Chess, Express, and Requests project graphs; 16, 32, and 64 representation units
claims.baseline: score-ranked exact nodes serialized with the same renderer at no greater token cost
guardrails: flat tokens no greater than candidate tokens
claims.minimum_effect: resolution-recall gain at least 0.02 on every frozen transfer project
claims.decision: no champion: GraphGraph and Requests passed, Chess and Express failed

claims.mechanism: A penalty proportional only to unresolved aggregate mass cancels when one internal cell is replaced entirely by internal children, so its coefficient cannot guide early hierarchy refinement.
claims.primary_metric: objective delta contributed by the mass term
guardrails: no leaf exposed by the split
claims.minimum_effect: exact algebraic cancellation plus deterministic plan test
claims.decision: reject coefficient tuning of a mass-only penalty as a remedy for early routing

claims.mechanism: Penalizing aggregate mass by normalized log cell size rewards every internal refinement and transfers useful resolution across projects.
claims.operating_regime: GraphGraph, Chess, Express, and Requests development/validation graphs; weights 0.001 through 1.0; 32 and 64 units
claims.decision: no formula champion; stop coefficient tuning and add a hard exact-frontier reserve

claims.mechanism: Exact-near and hierarchical-far representation allocates a fixed budget more effectively than flat retrieval.
claims.baseline: BM25, embedding top-k, BFS, flat PPR, production GraphGraph
claims.primary_metric: held-out oracle regret at equal serialized token cost

claims.mechanism: Hierarchy degrades resolution gradually as project size grows under fixed context budget.
claims.operating_regime: synthetic and real graphs across project-size strata
claims.primary_metric: quality slope against log node count

claims.mechanism: Residual propagation and hierarchy invalidation confine ordinary edit work to the affected region.
claims.operating_regime: non-hub edits, hub edits, moves, deletions, and refactors
claims.baseline: full rebuild and exact file splice
claims.primary_metric: dynamic work factor at bounded field error
claims.minimum_effect: materially below rebuild work for ordinary edits

claims.mechanism: Bridge, exception, and uncertainty reserves protect rare decisive evidence from aggregate smoothing.
claims.operating_regime: bridge, policy, security, rare-test, and lexical-adversary tasks
claims.minimum_effect: fewer catastrophic misses at small token premium

claims.mechanism: Better evidence approximation improves frozen-agent task outcomes when interpretation is controlled.
claims.operating_regime: repository completion and issue repair finalists
claims.baseline: production GraphGraph and strong lexical/vector baselines
claims.minimum_effect: statistically credible gain or equivalent quality at materially lower cost

claims.mechanism: Omitted-mass, distortion, and facet-gap receipts predict insufficient context.
claims.baseline: raw retrieval score and packet size
claims.primary_metric: Brier score and expected calibration error

claims.mechanism: Value-of-refinement allocates computation better than fixed hop or node budgets.
claims.operating_regime: direct, path, blast-radius, summary, change, and negative queries
claims.baseline: fixed hop and fixed node budgets
claims.minimum_effect: non-dominated in multiple query classes without guardrail regression

claims.mechanism: A model-agnostic core cover and receipt with thin protocol adapters transfers context-policy gains across unrelated model families.
claims.operating_regime: closed and open-weight model families, multiple context regimes, prompt and tool protocols, and multiple tokenizers
claims.primary_metric: cross-model quality-cost effect with per-family guardrails
claims.minimum_effect: positive held-out effect not attributable to one provider, or equivalent quality at materially lower total cost

claims.mechanism: Personalized PageRank over call/import direction reaches only the forward cone of a seed. Because 62.9% of active entities are directed sinks, the far field receives zero mass, so no multiresolution cover has anything to encode. Treating an edge as coupling both endpoints restores a graded field over the whole project.
claims.operating_regime: GraphGraph, Chess, Express, and Requests frozen Phase 1 graphs; the six Phase 1 tasks per project; damping 0.85, max_iter 30, tol 1e-7
claims.baseline: directed personalized PageRank (the incumbent field used by Phase 0 and Phase 1)
claims.primary_metric: median per-task support fraction of the influence field
guardrails: hierarchy, tasks, budgets, and metrics held fixed
claims.minimum_effect: median support fraction at or above 0.10 on every project
claims.decision: Directed coupling is degenerate on 3 of 4 projects (median support 0.0107%-0.0291%, zero mass outside the top 64 entities). Symmetric coupling is non-degenerate on 4 of 4 (median support 98.46%-99.95%, 62.5% of mass outside the top 64). Phase 1 therefore compared cover formulas over an empty far field on most projects; its formula-level conclusions do not isolate the formula. Re-run C1 and C1-HYBRID-RESERVE-003 under symmetric coupling before treating any cover verdict as final.

claims.mechanism: Symmetric coupling lets influence reach entities that are directed sinks, so field-ranked selection can surface a relevant callee, doc, or concept that forward-only diffusion never assigns any mass.
claims.operating_regime: GraphGraph, Chess, Express, and Requests frozen Phase 1 graphs; six tasks per project; token budgets 1024/2048/4096; pure field-ranked selection, not production search_nodes
claims.baseline: the same equal-token flat selection ranked by the directed field
claims.primary_metric: mean exact recall of the equal-token flat baseline
claims.minimum_effect: mean exact-recall gain at least 0.02 with more improved than regressed tasks
claims.decision: Symmetric coupling improved the flat baseline from mean exact recall 0.5035 to 0.5694 (median 0.2667 to 0.5000); paired across 72 cases 32 improved and 3 regressed. The reserve's own exact recall rose 0.4319 to 0.5206. Promising as a RETRIEVAL field, but measured on a pure field-ranked baseline, not on production search_nodes, which combines PPR with lexical, semantic, and kind signals and uses localized PPR on large graphs. Do not promote until measured on the production eval.

claims.mechanism: Production search_nodes combines PPR with lexical scoring, a degree boost, and kind priors. On queries that name their target symbol the lexical term determines the head of the ranking, and PPR only reorders the tail below the first hit.
claims.operating_regime: 21 resolvable labelled tasks across graphgraph-self, graphgraph-calibration, and graphgraph-doc-authority-target, scored on the live graph at limit 20
claims.primary_metric: mean recall and MRR through production search_nodes
guardrails: ranked lists must actually differ between arms
the directed arm must score identically to itself
claims.minimum_effect: any change in recall or first-hit MRR
claims.decision: Disabling PPR entirely scores identically to every coupling: recall 0.6905, MRR 0.6905. All 21 ranked lists do change, so the term is wired and active -- it reorders the tail, not the head. Field-stage work has no measurable leverage on the tasks this project gates against. Do not tune the field further until a paraphrase/conceptual task set exists that can detect its contribution.

candidates.algorithm: Current GraphGraph anchors, routing, expansion, selection, and packet rendering.
Exhaustive dynamic program minimizing uniform-cell squared error over hierarchy antichains.
candidates.complexity: oracle-only exact tree dynamic program, pseudo-polynomial in the integer representation budget

candidates.algorithm: Exact local frontier plus deterministic containment hierarchy and explicit exception reserve.
Deterministic bounded-arity path hierarchy with one-step greedy minimization of cell L2 reconstruction error plus 0.01 times unresolved aggregate mass.
candidates.complexity: linear-size hierarchy; warm self-project compilation approximately 0.2-0.6 seconds by budget
candidates.decision: rejected as cross-project champion; retain hierarchy and renderer as reusable experimental components

candidates.algorithm: Bounded-arity path hierarchy minimizing L2 plus a swept coefficient times aggregate mass times normalized log cell size.
candidates.complexity: offline four-weight sweep took approximately 530 seconds; one frozen configuration remains subsecond warm
candidates.decision: rejected: every swept configuration had negative worst-project gain and failed exact-recall guardrails

candidates.algorithm: Reserve a hard token fraction for score-ranked exact entities, represent the remaining project with aggregate cells that explicitly subtract those sparse exceptions, then optimize only the residual budget.
candidates.complexity: moderate; requires exception-aware cover receipts and token-budget rather than unit-budget compilation
candidates.exposure: opt-in --representation hybrid on context/query/final; default remains flat; absent from the MCP surface
candidates.gate_status: EXP-GPA-HYBRID-RESERVE ran and FAILED under both couplings: worst-project median resolution gain +0.0000 against a required +0.02. Aggregate cells buy a mean resolution credit of only +0.028 (directed) / +0.012 (symmetric). Not promotable.
candidates.observed: Symmetric coupling makes the far field real (aggregate mass 0.0 -> 0.43-0.61, refinements 0 -> 5-7) but does not make the representation win: it raises the equal-token flat baseline faster than it raises the reserve.

candidates.algorithm: Localized residual Personalized PageRank under the C1 cover.
Heat-kernel diffusion with preregistered diffusion-time sweep under the C1 cover.
Diverse semantic landmarks with explicit approximation residual.
Analytic value-of-refinement controller and iterative cell expansion.
Repeatedly expand the currently feasible cell with maximum immediate L2 reduction per representation unit.
candidates.fallback: exact dynamic program on oracle graphs; fixed threshold or bounded search in production research
candidates.complexity: low, but no universal optimality guarantee
candidates.decision: rejected as an optimal controller; retained as a runtime baseline

candidates.algorithm: Diffuse the query-conditioned field over the symmetrized edge set: every active edge contributes both its own orientation and its reverse, preserving weight, confidence, and provenance. All downstream stages consume the field unchanged.
candidates.complexity: low; one pure field-construction stage with no downstream change. Costs one extra edge list per compile and leaves preprocessing, hierarchy, and packet syntax untouched.
candidates.observed: Clears the substrate gate on 4/4 projects and improves field-ranked retrieval (+0.066 mean exact recall, 32 better / 3 worse paired). Costs one cached edge-list rebuild plus ~6x PPR time. Not yet measured on production search_nodes.
candidates.gate_status: Clears the substrate gate and improves a bare field-ranked baseline, but EXP-GPA-COUPLING-PROD found no recall or MRR change through production search_nodes at 11.9x latency. Not promotable.

candidates.algorithm: Diffuse the field over reversed edges only, spreading influence to dependents rather than dependencies.
candidates.complexity: low; same stage as F1-SYMMETRIC-COUPLING with a different orientation
candidates.gate_status: no production leverage; same verdict as F1 at lower cost
